spec.full_target: Let n,m be positive integers, u:ℝ^n×(0,∞)→ℝ^m jointly smooth, and q∈ℝ^m have Euclidean norm one. Assume for all x∈ℝ^n and t>0, |u(x,t)|=1; for every (x,t) there exists a(x,t)∈ℝ with u_tt(x,t)−Δ_xu(x,t)=a(x,t)u(x,t), with no regularity of a assumed; and for every finite closed interval J⊂(0,∞) there exists compact C_J⊂ℝ^n such that u(x,t)=q for all x∉C_J and t∈J. Define e(x,t)=||u_t(x,t)||²+Σ_{j=1}^n||∂_{x_j}u(x,t)||² and E(t)=∫_{ℝ^n}e(x,t)dx using Lebesgue measure, Euclidean vector norms, and the Frobenius/Hilbert–Schmidt spatial-gradient square; Δ_x is the componentwise sum of second spatial derivatives. Prove e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable for every t>0, E is differentiable at every t>0, and E'(t)=0. No endpoint t=0 assertion is included.
spec.conclusion: For every r>0, e(·,r) is Lebesgue integrable, E is differentiable at r, and E'(r)=0.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary r>0. The first direct input states that e(·,r) is Lebesgue integrable, so E(r) is the ordinary finite integral from D002. The second direct input states that E is differentiable at r and E′(r)=∫e_t(x,r)dx.

N003 gives E′(r)=2∫_{ℝⁿ} h(x) dx, where h(x)=u_t(x,r)·(u_{tt}(x,r)−Δ_xu(x,r)). N004 says h(x)=0 for every x, so this integrand is the identically zero real-valued function. Apply M015 with X=ℝⁿ, μ=Lebesgue measure and V=ℝ: its whole-space integral is zero. Hence E′(r)=0. Together with N001 and N002 this proves all three clauses for arbitrary r>0.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary t>0, set J=[t/2,3t/2], and use H003 to choose compact C such that u(x,s)=q for every x∉C and s∈J. The complement of C is open, and u is constant q on its spatial neighborhood for all s∈J. Smoothness therefore implies every first derivative in x and t, as well as the mixed derivatives entering e_t, vanishes off C. The fields u_t,u_{x_j},e,e_t are continuous by smoothness and supported in C. In particular e(·,t) is continuous with compact support. Euclidean opens are measurable, Lebesgue measure is finite on compact sets, and ℝ is a normed additive commutative group; M001 gives integrability of e(·,t). This proves the claimed support and integrability facts for arbitrary t.

argument.text: Differentiate H001 in time: 2u·u_t=0, hence u·u_t=0. H002 supplies a scalar a at this point with u_{tt}−Δ_xu=a u. Dot with u_t to obtain u_t·(u_{tt}−Δ_xu)=a(u_t·u)=0. No regularity of a is used.

Let J=[r/2,3r/2] and choose compact C from H003. To cover the allowed empty-C case, set C*=C∪{0}; this is compact and nonempty, and u=q outside C* throughout J because outside C* implies outside C. Thus the derivative fields, including e_t, vanish outside C*. By M005, C*×J is compact and nonempty. M004 applied to continuous e_t gives uniform continuity on C*×J. Choose δ>0 so points within δ have e_t values differing by less than 1; the δ/2-balls centered at all points of C*×J cover it, and compactness gives a finite subcover with at least one center p_i. Therefore K=1+max_i |e_t(p_i)| is a well-defined finite nonnegative bound for |e_t| on C*×J. Off C*, e_t=0, so |e_t(x,τ)|≤K·1_{C*}(x) for every x and τ∈J. Since C* is compact, it is measurable and has finite Lebesgue measure; M008 gives integrability on C* of the constant K and M009 gives integrability of b=K·1_{C*} on ℝⁿ. For F(τ)(x)=e(x,τ) and F′(τ)(x)=e_t(x,τ), continuity gives strong measurability, and N001 gives F(r) integrable. Smoothness gives the pointwise parameter derivative; the bound above is uniform in τ∈J. The interval (r/2,3r/2) is a neighborhood of r. Thus the hypotheses of M006 hold and E is differentiable at r with E′(r)=∫e_t(x,r)dx. Since r was arbitrary, this holds for every positive time.

argument.text: Fix r>0. N001 supplies a compact C and a closed time window containing r in its interior such that u=q outside C throughout that window, with the first time and spatial derivatives supported in C. For every spatial index j, put f(x)=∂_{x_j}u(x,r), g(x)=u_t(x,r), and v equal to the jth Euclidean coordinate vector. Smoothness and constancy of u off C imply f,g and their first Frechet derivatives are continuous and vanish off C; thus the three scalar products B(f′(x)v,g(x)), B(f(x),g′(x)v), B(f(x),g(x)) are continuous and compactly supported. By the ambient Euclidean finite-on-compacts property and M001 they are integrable. The derivative identities hold everywhere by smoothness, hence in particular on the required topological supports. Apply M011 with B the Euclidean inner product to obtain ∫∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t=−∫∂_{x_jx_j}u·u_t. Summing over j and using the finite-dimensional product rule gives ∫e_t=2∫u_t·(u_{tt}−Δ_xu). N002 identifies E′(r) with ∫e_t, yielding the stated formula for arbitrary r>0.
